II21A-01.note: Two reversed pairs: A/D restate or reverse the shared near/far pattern (fit both accounts), B/C split on the discriminator. Test-wise student strikes A/D, then picks the warm-dry (upslope) group; B is the tempting reversal.

II21A-02.note: Three habitats must be tracked; pools vs riffles holds crayfish constant and varies oxygen. D (pools vs backwaters) is the tempting one but supports Dufresne; B fits both.

II21A-03.note: Same two-reversed-pair template as A-01: A restates the north/south pattern, C reverses it, B/D split on the pike-only vs weeds-only habitats. B is the tempting reversal.

II21A-04.note: Key compares Corlan (drop 6) with the most tolerant greenhouse variety, Dalmi (drop 8); D is the off-claim field variety and C the weakest greenhouse. A (Bexa, drop 9, higher after-value 84) also shows Corlan beating a greenhouse variety, so only 'closest competitor' logic separates A from B.

II21A-05.note: Only C crosses the backswimmer condition (present vs absent); A compares two present ponds, B and D two absent ponds. Temperature is near-constant, so the confound is inert; reading one column decides it.

II21A-06.note: Requires ratios: Corvane 0.80 vs Abrisk 0.75 (next best), Eskelin 0.65, Belloway 0.60, Dunmarra 0.50. Strong trap: Abrisk's and Belloway's higher absolute salt-water masses make A look wrong to a student comparing raw mg.

II21B-01.note: Same template: D restates age-cracking pattern, B reverses it, A/C reversed pair on valley vs plateau. Key = group with the hypothesized factor and less of the rival's, named in the 'however' sentence.

II21B-02.note: Same template: D restates the late-summer peak, B reverses it, A/C reversed pair on northern (cool, fertilized) vs southern bays. C is the tempting reversal.

II21B-03.note: Ridges dying more than hollows contradicts CO2 pooling while fitting drought. A supports Haskins (tempting for a student who misses 'weaken'); B fits both; C is irrelevant and strikable.

II21B-04.note: Specific energy: prototype 150 Wh/kg vs J 140, L 160, K 230, H 120. A is sodium-ion (off-claim, strikable on sight); D is tempting because L stores more and 160 is close to 150.

II21B-05.note: C is the only option naming a white membrane roof; A, B, D are other surfaces and fall on reading the Surface column. Juniper's 'Coated white metal' is the only lure. C cites only one of the two membranes (the higher one), acceptable as best available.

II21B-06.note: Needs the 1,400 m threshold: Kestow (above) is milder than Halvern (below). A (both above) and B (both below) are tempting because the warmer value comes first; C crosses the threshold but runs the wrong way.

II21C-01.note: Same template: D restates older/newer pattern, B reverses it, A/C reversed pair on Marwick (long-tenure renters) vs Ronsdale (new owners).

II21C-02.note: Mosby vs Renfield holds 'moved' constant and varies distance, so it undercuts confusion-not-distance. D fits both (strikable); B and C support Ortega, and C is tempting for a student who confuses which claim to weaken.

II21C-03.note: Same template: C restates casual/formal pattern, D reverses it, A/B reversed pair on council (fast, formal) vs market (slow, casual). A is the tempting reversal.

II21C-04.note: Key compares with the smallest raise among under-100 co-ops (Pruett 0.45). A (Marlow, 310 members) is off-claim but has the closest value; B and C are in-group but not the binding comparison. 'Closest in-group competitor' template.

II21C-05.note: Redvale (76) is the highest standard classroom; C (Mercer, visual) is off-claim with the closest value; A and D are weaker in-group comparisons. Same closest-competitor template.

II21C-06.note: Only Ostler is in the program and fell below half (38 to 17). B (Northby) falls below half but is not in the program, the main lure; A and D fall but not by half, which requires arithmetic to reject.

II21D-01.note: Same template: D restates the over-time increase, B reverses it, A/C reversed pair on lowland (route) vs upland (mines). A is the tempting reversal.

II21D-02.note: Sorle lower (salt, mild floods) collapsing more than Tyrne upper (violent floods, no salt) pits the factors against each other. B, C (within-river lower vs upper) and D fit both; C is the most tempting since Sorle floods are mild.

II21D-03.note: D holds storage constant (dry) and varies iron beaters. B is the strong lure: Wyrlow vs Tamsby but confounded by damp vs dry. A supports Yarrow; C compares two wood-beaten papers.

II21D-04.note: B is the only pair that holds decade constant and varies window direction. A is the lure (south vs north but confounded by age); C and D vary only age and are strikable once the confound sentence is read.

II21D-05.note: Tidewater (7,800) is the best-selling installment novel; A (Vesper Lane, complete volume) is off-claim with the closest value. Same closest-in-group-competitor template as C-04, C-05, A-04.

II21D-06.note: Gains: Stelmond +200 vs never-Sunday Wexmoor +120 (largest), Tolvane +60, Zaltby -40. A (Ullerby +180) and B are Sunday-opening and off-claim; D (Tolvane) tempts by larger absolute membership. Requires subtraction.
